speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. Please tell me, how long have you been experiencing wrist pain, fever, and these skin lesions?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That history of self-resolving knee pain and your recent camping trip in Minnesota are very concerning; given the wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions, could you describe exactly what the rash looks like and where it is located? Also, have you noticed any joint swelling or redness in your knees or wrists right now?

REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, ESR, CRP, and blood cultures.
REQUEST IMAGES: Photos of the skin lesions.

speaker: Doctor
text: The lab results show a markedly elevated white blood cell count in your wrist fluid and a Gram stain revealing Gram-negative diplococci, which strongly suggests a bacterial joint infection. The painless violaceous lesions on your hands are also concerning for a systemic infectious process; could you confirm if you have any recent tick bites, animal scratches, or if anyone else in your household is sick?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The lab results showing Gram-negative diplococci in the wrist fluid are highly specific for *Neisseria gonorrhoeae*, which explains your joint infection and the skin lesions consistent with disseminated gonococcal infection. Given your sexual history, this fits perfectly; do you have any history of penile or urethral discharge?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Disseminated Gonococcal Infection
